courseTitle: Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) for Data Scientists

slots.practicalActivity: Reproduce the lesson's silent-failure demo on the churn model: feed it the test set unchanged, then with monthly_spend multiplied by 100 (a unit bug), then with support_calls bumped by 2 (a drift stand-in), and confirm accuracy collapses from 0.768 to 0.260 on the unit bug while the drift case only slips to 0.728 with a rising mean predicted risk. Then turn the same workflow into lifecycle.py with prepare()/train()/evaluate() functions, a fixed random seed, and a validation gate that only saves the model when accuracy clears 0.75, running it twice to confirm identical output both times.
slots.deliverable: Printed accuracy/mean-churn-probability for all 3 scenarios (as-trained, cents bug, drift stand-in) showing the collapse, plus a working lifecycle.py whose two runs print byte-identical prepare/evaluate/validate output.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the full churn-project folder tree (churn/ package with __init__.py, data.py, model.py, train.py; plus data/raw/, models/, notebooks/, scripts/, tests/, params.yaml, requirements.txt), moving the load_data/split_data/build_pipeline logic from your notebook into the importable churn/ package. Read settings from params.yaml, run python -m churn.train from the project root, and confirm the printed accuracy matches your earlier notebook result exactly.
slots.deliverable: The committed-ready churn-project folder tree with code in the churn/ package, and a terminal run of python -m churn.train whose accuracy output matches the original notebook's number.

slots.practicalActivity: Run git init in your churn-project, use git status --short -uall to see everything about to be committed (including data, models, and __pycache__), then write a .gitignore excluding data/, models/*.joblib, and caches, confirming the exclusions with git check-ignore -v. Install nbstripout and show a notebook diff before and after the filter strips execution-count noise. Finally, create a tune-C branch, change params.yaml's C to 10.0, retrain, and commit with a message that ties the setting to the resulting accuracy, then read git diff main to see both the settings and results change together.
slots.deliverable: A .gitignore with a check-ignore confirmation for 2 ignored paths, a before/after nbstripout diff on one notebook, and a tune-C branch commit whose git diff main shows both the C value and accuracy changing together.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a requirements.txt pinning only your 4 direct dependencies (no numpy pin), install it into a fresh virtual environment, and reproduce the lesson's real failure: a numpy.dtype binary-incompatibility ValueError even though pip check reports nothing broken. Fix it by pinning numpy explicitly, freeze the working environment to requirements.lock, then build a second brand-new virtual environment from the lock file and diff its pip freeze output against the lock file to prove it rebuilds identically and reproduces the same accuracy.
slots.deliverable: The captured ValueError from the unpinned-numpy environment, the working requirements.lock file, and a diff output (empty) proving a from-scratch rebuild matches it exactly, with the same training accuracy both times.

slots.practicalActivity: Install DVC, run dvc init, and run dvc add data/raw/customers.csv to create the .dvc pointer file, committing it to Git. Append 200 rows to the CSV, run dvc status and dvc add again to see the pointer's hash change, then use git checkout <old-commit> -- data/raw/customers.csv.dvc followed by dvc checkout to time-travel back to the 1,000-row version, and forward again to 1,200 rows. Set up a local folder as a DVC remote and run dvc push then dvc pull after deleting your local cache, confirming the file comes back correctly.
slots.deliverable: Two committed .dvc pointer versions with different md5 hashes, a dvc diff output between the two commits, and a confirmed dvc pull recovery of the data after deleting your local cache.

slots.practicalActivity: Write churn/versioning.py with a file_hash() SHA-256 function and a save_versioned() helper that writes a churn.meta.json sidecar recording the model hash, the data's md5, the hyperparameters, metrics, and library versions. Train with C=1.0 three times and confirm you get a byte-identical model hash every time, then train once with C=0.1 and confirm a different hash. Track both with DVC, tag them model-v1 and model-v2 in Git, and use git diff model-v1 model-v2 -- models/churn.meta.json to see exactly what changed.
slots.deliverable: Three training runs proving C=1.0 reproduces the identical model hash while C=0.1 does not, both versions tracked with DVC and tagged in Git, and a git diff output isolating the single changed setting and metric.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a tracked training function that logs git_commit/data_version/stage tags, C and split_seed params, train_ and test_ prefixed metrics, and the fitted model as an MLflow artifact. Run it for 6 values of C plus one deliberately broken run with C=-1, confirming the broken run is still recorded with status FAILED instead of being lost. Use mlflow.search_runs with a FINISHED filter to compare all 6 real runs by test_roc_auc, and separately run mlflow.sklearn.autolog() on the same pipeline to see why its training_roc_auc numbers should never be trusted as test performance.
slots.deliverable: A 6-row MLflow comparison table sorted by test_roc_auc, confirmation that the C=-1 run is recorded as FAILED rather than missing, and a side-by-side note contrasting autolog's training_ metrics with your own logged test_ metrics.

slots.practicalActivity: Register 2 of your lesson-8 runs (C=1.0 and C=10.0) under one name in a local MLflow registry, tagging each version with its test_roc_auc and a validation_status of pending. Set a champion alias on version 1 and a challenger alias on version 2, load models:/cancel-risk-model@champion and confirm it scores correctly, then promote by re-pointing champion to version 2 and roll back by pointing it to version 1 again. Finally, deliberately delete the version currently behind the champion alias and confirm loading by that alias now fails, exactly as the lesson warns.
slots.deliverable: Two registered versions with tags, a working promotion (re-pointing champion) and rollback (one-line alias move), and a captured failure when loading an alias whose version was deleted while still referenced.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the FastAPI churn service with a lifespan handler that loads the model once at startup, a Pydantic Customer model with field-level range and Literal validation, a /health endpoint, and a /predict endpoint returning churn_probability, churn_predicted, and model_version. Run it with uvicorn, curl a high-risk customer (short tenure, no autopay, several tickets) and a loyal customer, then send a request with contract="weekly" and a request missing fields, confirming both are rejected with 422 before reaching the model, and browse the auto-generated /docs page.
slots.deliverable: Captured curl responses for a high-risk and a low-risk customer (probabilities close to the documented 0.909 and 0.007), plus the 2 captured 422 validation-error responses for the bad contract value and the missing fields.

slots.practicalActivity: Write a Dockerfile for your churn API that pins scikit-learn==1.1.2 on a python:3.10-slim base, copies requirements before code for layer caching, creates and switches to a non-root user, and uses the exec-form CMD. Confirm with pip download that scikit-learn==1.1.2 has no Python-3.11 wheel but does have one for 3.10, which is why the base image version matters. If Docker is available, build and run the image, curl its /health and /predict, and confirm the churn probability matches your lesson-10 local uvicorn run exactly.
slots.deliverable: A working Dockerfile with a .dockerignore, the pip-download evidence that pins the Python base-image version choice, and (if Docker is available) a running container whose /predict answer matches the local server's answer exactly.

slots.practicalActivity: Time 3 ways of scoring the same churn model on your own machine: one vectorized batch call over a large table, one row-by-row predict_proba call repeated 200 times, and 200 HTTP requests against your running FastAPI server, reproducing the lesson's microseconds-per-prediction comparison and its log-scale chart. Build the monthly call-list batch job (score every customer, tag with model_version and scored_on, keep the top 20% by risk) and write a platform-agnostic smoke-test script that checks /health and then verifies a known golden customer's probability is within 0.005 of the expected value, confirming it fails loudly against a dead URL.
slots.deliverable: A table of measured per-prediction cost for batch, in-process, and HTTP scoring, the generated call_list.csv from the batch job, and a smoke-test script that passes against your running server and fails with a clear connection error against a bad URL.

slots.practicalActivity: Set up pytest.ini and conftest.py with session-scoped data and model fixtures, then write the 3 layers of tests from the lesson: data tests (schema, no missing values, positive charges, known categories), a training smoke test on a small synthetic sample, and 3 model-behavior tests (more support tickets never lowers risk, an unseen category never crashes the model, a golden customer scores within tolerance). Run the full suite to confirm it passes, then deliberately corrupt 3 cells in churn.csv (a negative charge, an invalid contract label, a missing tenure) and rerun to see exactly which named tests fail.
slots.deliverable: A passing pytest run (all tests green) followed by a second run against corrupted data showing the specific named test failures, proving each assumption is independently checked.

slots.practicalActivity: Write .github/workflows/ci.yml with a test job (checkout, setup-python pinned to 3.10, pip-cached install, train, pytest) and a package job that depends on it and only runs on main, validating the file parses correctly with PyYAML. Write a small local runner that executes the test job's run: steps in a fresh checkout of your project, and fix the real bug the lesson found (a missing models/ folder causing FileNotFoundError) with one line. Finally, simulate a bad pull request by weakening the model's regularization and confirm the golden-customer test from lesson 14 fails even though overall AUC barely changes.
slots.deliverable: A validated ci.yml workflow file, the one-line fix for the FileNotFoundError bug found by your local runner, and a captured test run showing the golden-customer test failing on the simulated bad pull request.

slots.practicalActivity: Write validate.py with the lesson's 4 rules (an absolute AUC floor, no more than a small drop versus production, a per-contract-type slice floor, and a calibration check), and run it against 3 real candidates: one retrained with the same recipe (should pass all checks), one with the contract column dropped (should fail only the vs_production check), and one with stronger regularization (should pass inside tolerance). Then build the lesson's file-based registry with register()/promote()/rollback(), and reproduce its full promotion trace: a refused straight-to-production attempt, a refused self-approval, a successful approval by a different approver, a refused promotion of a validation-failed candidate, and a one-line rollback to the previous production version.
slots.deliverable: A validation report for all 3 candidates showing exactly which checks each one passes or fails, plus a promotion-trace log reproducing all 5 refuse/approve/rollback outcomes from your own registry script.

slots.practicalActivity: Implement psi() and ks() in drift.py, then build a drifted production batch where days_idle and sessions_30d are scaled and relabeled, running the drift report across all 6 features and confirming PSI flags only the 2 shifted ones while the other 4 stay quiet (below 0.1). Then build a concept-drift batch with the same input distribution but a new, price-driven cancellation rule, and confirm every feature's PSI stays near zero while AUC collapses toward random, proving a silent drift report does not mean a healthy model.
slots.deliverable: A 6-feature drift report (PSI and KS) correctly flagging the 2 shifted features and clearing the other 4, plus a second report showing all-quiet PSI alongside a collapsed AUC on the concept-drift batch.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the 8-simulated-week monitor from model_utils.py and make_week(), computing a weekly report of AUC, mean predicted risk vs. actual rate, top-20% precision, and max PSI, and reproduce the lesson's pattern of an early drift-only period (weeks 3-4) followed by a performance collapse (weeks 5-8). Apply the AUC-floor, calibration-gap, and PSI alert rules to all 8 weeks, then add a 2-consecutive-breach requirement before paging and confirm it correctly suppresses the shaky first breach while still catching the real decline.
slots.deliverable: An 8-week monitoring table with all 4 tracked metrics, a raw alert log, and a second, persistence-filtered alert log showing one fewer false page than the raw version.

slots.practicalActivity: Write retrain_decision() combining a 14-day cooldown, a 2-consecutive-week performance breach trigger, a 90-day schedule trigger, a labelled-data-volume gate, and a drift-only "investigate" branch, then run it across the same 8 simulated weeks from the previous lesson and confirm it produces hold/investigate/retrain exactly as the lesson describes. Run retrain_and_compare() training a candidate on weeks 5-6 and judging it on weeks 7-8, and write one honest sentence about what it means that the candidate beats the champion yet still falls below the floor.
slots.deliverable: An 8-week action log (hold/investigate/retrain) from your own decision function, and the retrain_and_compare() output with a written judgment on whether the improved-but-still-failing candidate should ship.

slots.practicalActivity: Write fingerprint() to hash a training DataFrame and subgroup_report() to compute cancel rate, AUC, and flagged share by a categorical column, then run it by plan and by channel, flagging the smallest segment's result as uncertain rather than a verdict. Assemble a model_card.json with intended_use, out_of_scope, the training-data fingerprint, metrics, limitations, and monitoring thresholds pulled from your own lesson-19 numbers, and append one approval event to an append-only audit_log.jsonl file.
slots.deliverable: A subgroup report by plan and by channel with group sizes noted, a complete model_card.json, and an audit_log.jsonl with at least one appended approval event.

lessons.title: Capstone Kickoff: Automate a Model's Full Lifecycle

slots.practicalActivity: Write params.yaml with the gate floors (min_auc, min_ap, max_drop), drift threshold, and retrain settings (min_age_days, min_rows, breach_weeks) exactly as the kickoff specifies, before writing any pipeline code. Scaffold the full churn-project tree (churn/ modules for data, model, gate, registry, serve, contract, drift, retrain, pipeline; tests/; .github/workflows/lifecycle.yml), implement load_split() and build_pipeline()/evaluate(), and run the baseline to confirm it matches the kickoff's own numbers (4,800/1,200 split, ROC AUC 0.744, average precision 0.333) comfortably above your written floors.
slots.deliverable: The committed params.yaml with gate/drift/retrain thresholds, the scaffolded 6-stage project tree, and a baseline run printing ROC AUC and average precision above your own written floors.

slots.practicalActivity: Implement and run all 6 lifecycle stages end to end: train and log to a local MLflow store, run the validation_gate pure function, register the version and only set the champion alias after every check passes, serve it behind a standard-library HTTP contract test, run the PSI/KS drift check, and call retrain_decision(). Wire them together in run_cycle() and run it once from an empty registry, confirming you get a clean "promoted" result with version 2, the same outcome the lesson's own run produced.
slots.deliverable: Working implementations of all 6 stage functions, and a run_cycle() execution printing "promoted" with the new version number, matching the chapter's own result.

slots.practicalActivity: Run run_lifecycle.py end to end across the initial model, 8 simulated weeks of drift and decline, a triggered retrain that is correctly blocked at the gate, and a scheduled refresh that is promoted, reproducing the chapter's full cycle-1/cycle-2-blocked/cycle-3-promoted trace. Then run both safety drills: shuffle the training labels and confirm the gate blocks the resulting model with all 3 documented reasons, and wrap the champion so it returns percentages instead of probabilities and confirm the contract test catches the out-of-range value. Finish by writing the illustrative GitHub Actions lifecycle.yml (validated with PyYAML, not run on GitHub) and assembling a README that leads with the blocked-gate and drill results.
slots.deliverable: A full run_lifecycle.py execution log reproducing all 3 cycles, captured output from both safety drills proving the champion never moved, the parses-clean lifecycle.yml workflow file, and a portfolio README that leads with the proof that the safety gates actually block bad models.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can take a model from a notebook to a production system with real engineering discipline — versioned data and models, tracked experiments, a packaged and containerized prediction service, automated tests and CI/CD gates, and drift detection with retraining triggers — and has a working, self-built, end-to-end automated model lifecycle to show as a portfolio project.
